title: PowerPoint for Mac: Copilot edits presentations through chat for Copilot Chat users
summary: Hold: Microsoft's PowerPoint editing documentation says editing is on by default in the prompt box, rather than an experience users must opt into. The administration paths and automation are supported, and the briefing correctly reports the conflicting licensing statements.

claims.where: What's changing: second paragraph; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The sources do not describe an administrator enablement step before a user can ask Copilot to edit.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot PowerPoint disable editing admin approval policy Mac agent mode'. Read roadmap, overview, Mac preferences and Edit with Copilot in PowerPoint; the latter says it is on by default in the prompt box and tells users to open Copilot Chat.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing: each user chooses to ask Copilot for an edit
claims.claim: The feature's default state is user-opt-in.
claims.quote: Copilot is an AI-powered assistant available in PowerPoint for Windows, Mac, and the web. It can be accessed by opening Copilot Chat using the Copilot icon at the bottom-right corner of the screen. It is on by default in the prompt box.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to "on". Replace "Neither source describes a step an administrator must take before users can use it; each user chooses to ask Copilot for an edit" with "Microsoft's Edit with Copilot in PowerPoint page says it is on by default in the prompt box; users ask for changes through Copilot Chat." Cite and add https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/008f17aa-8e5f-4cda-ba6c-0588000bdad7 to sources.

claims.where: controls[1].ui and controls[1].api; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no administrator switch specifically for Copilot editing in PowerPoint for Mac alone.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot PowerPoint disable editing admin approval policy Mac agent mode'; 'PowerPoint Mac Copilot editing admin switch approval fair use limits'. Read Mac preferences, Cloud Policy overview, Copilot overview and search excerpts; no editing-only admin switch.

claims.claim: No new sign-in, permission or connector is described specifically for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: '557276 Copilot PowerPoint'; 'Copilot PowerPoint disable editing admin approval policy Mac agent mode'. Read roadmap, overview and Edit with Copilot in PowerPoint; no new feature-specific sign-in, permission or connector is described.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no administrator-required approval step before Copilot writes changes to the presentation.
claims.quote: Searched: 'PowerPoint Copilot editing administrator require approval before changes'. Read roadmap, editing Support page and results. SharePoint content approval governs publication visibility, not approval before Copilot writes; no such editing approval control found.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Disabling content-analyzing connected experiences removes Copilot features from Excel, OneNote, Outlook, PowerPoint and Word on Mac, not editing alone.
claims.quote: If you turn off connected experiences that analyze your content ... Microsoft Copilot features won't be available ... Excel ... OneNote ... Outlook ... PowerPoint ... Word. This applies ... the most current version ... Windows, Mac, iOS, or Android devices.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: rendered first row
claims.claim: The printed Microsoft 365 Apps admin center route reaches Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content.
claims.quote: Cloud Policy overview: Under Customization, select Policy Management. ... Policy configurations ... Create ... Start with the basics ... Choose the scope ... Configure Settings. Mac preferences: Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content.

claims.claim: OfficeExperiencesAnalyzingContentPreference can be set to FALSE in com.microsoft.office and enforced through a Configuration Profile or MDM.
claims.quote: enforced through a Configuration Profile or Mobile Device Management (MDM) server. ... Preference Domain: com.microsoft.office; Key: OfficeExperiencesAnalyzingContentPreference; Data Type: Boolean; Possible values: TRUE (enabled) FALSE (disabled)

claims.claim: Users cannot change the preference when it is enforced.
claims.quote: When the preferences are enforced, the user can't change the values, and any in-app controls will appear disabled.

claims.claim: When the content-analysis preference is unset, these connected experiences are available.
claims.quote: If you don't set this preference, connected experiences that analyze content are available to users.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy settings take precedence over preference settings.
claims.quote: policy settings implemented by using Cloud Policy take precedence over policy settings implemented by using Group Policy on Windows Server, and taking precedence over preference settings or locally applied policy settings.

claims.claim: BlockContentAnalysisServices excludes labelled content from Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook.
claims.quote: Support for this setting differs for clients and apps. Identify the minimum versions of Office that support this setting by using the capabilities tables ... content with the configured sensitivity label will be excluded from Microsoft 365 Copilot in the named Office apps
claims.fix: Qualify the Risk assessment sentence as: "On Office clients that support the setting, a sensitivity label with the advanced setting BlockContentAnalysisServices excludes labelled content from Microsoft 365 Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook."
